headline: A
label: JevBench v1.6.10 · fresh regular draw v1.6-regular-20261012, 4 new self-hosted systems
measurement_notes: Refusals, errors and context-bound failures stay in the full 1,500 denominator. Every row kept its own package, model, runtime and context settings; nothing was re-run for presentation.

NOT DIRECTLY COMPARABLE WITH THE LIVE v1.6.1 BOARD OR WITH THE EARLIER FRESH DRAWS. This release is a different draw with its own small-field median: G_med = 9.839526770355711 over 4 members, against 2.573387642438244 on the live field. G_med_flag_gt10 is false. The gap penalty is max(0, 1 - max(0, (gap - G_med) - 8)/100), so this field's threshold is G_med + 8 = 17.84. On the merged live board this draw is placed with offset 0 while its anchor runs are pending, exactly like the two earlier fresh draws. Measured, not estimated: re-scored at the live field's median 2.573387642438244, standard_one_3b_sh Intelligence 32.786 would be 31.294 and metask_jev_rain_12b_trained 67.826 would be 67.587; krino-2b and metask_jev_rain_31b_trained are unchanged (receipt LIVE-MEDIAN-SENSITIVITY-R99.json).

Cost: no item is excluded from the cost basis on this draw. Every row is priced from its own measured usage block at a clearly-labelled ESTIMATE rate fixed before scoring (r99 pre-registration); none is a bill any of these systems issued. Every row is under the published v1.6 cost ceiling of USD 0.0646 per 1,000 decisions. The cost normalizer C0 is USD 0.001 per 1,000 decisions with 30 cost points per decade.

No subject-topic radar in this release: this draw's items have not been topic-labelled yet, and the shared topic labels of earlier draws do not cover its items. Families, use cases and languages are authoring metadata and are shown.

krino-2b: All 1,500 items answered HTTP 200 with native probabilities. The 15 longest items of the draw (the same 15 that standard_one_3b_sh refuses) ran with the state truncated to 65,536 tokens, as the author's submitted serve command documents (KEV_TRUNCATE_STATES=1); every other item is at most 1,802 input tokens. Reference kernels were used (KEV_FUSED=0) because the documented pip install has no flash-linear-attention. Kev reports usage.output_tokens as the token count of the serialized answer JSON although nothing is generated (165,276 over 1,500 decisions); it is priced as reported at the frozen DeepInfra Qwen/Qwen3.5-2B reference, USD 0.02/0.10 per 1M. Measured on an evaluator-owned Lium H100 pod in an offline container (network none).

metask_jev_rain_12b_trained: All 1,500 items answered HTTP 200. The author's service runs the authors' own int4 (W4A16) quantization of Google's Gemma 4 12B QAT checkpoint with their own rank-16 LoRA applied unmerged by vLLM; per its model card it takes a second pass on part of the items, so it reports generated output tokens (84,238 over 1,500 decisions) and its latency has a long tail (raw p95 8.1 s against a raw p50 of 0.13 s). Measured on an evaluator-owned Lium H100 80GB pod (IP geolocated to Nizhny Novgorod, Russia) in an offline container (network none). google/gemma-4-12b-it is not listed on OpenRouter, so the cost uses the nearest listed sibling, google/gemma-3-12b-it at USD 0.05/0.15 per 1M, times its own usage. It is a different system from the earlier metask_jev_rain_12b row.

metask_jev_rain_31b_trained: All 1,500 items answered HTTP 200. The author's service runs Google's unchanged W4A16 Gemma 4 31B QAT checkpoint with the authors' own rank-16 LoRA applied unmerged by vLLM, at max_model_len 6,656 (per the measuring operator's handoff): longer inputs are shortened by the service's own documented extraction rule rather than refused, so the longest items were answered on a shortened state. The authors tested it on H200; it was measured on an evaluator-owned Lium H100 80GB pod (IP geolocated to Nizhny Novgorod, Russia) in an offline container (network none) with unchanged settings. The service reports 1 output token per decision; cost is the OpenRouter google/gemma-4-31b-it list price (USD 0.09/0.34 per 1M) times its own usage.

standard_one_3b_sh: 15 of 1,500 items returned HTTP 422: they are the longest items of the draw (at least 108,865 characters; every answered item is at most 13,495) and exceed the model's documented 32,768-token context, so the author's server refuses them rather than truncating; scored wrong per method. Measured on an evaluator-owned Lium H100 pod in an offline container (network none). Priced at the M2 base-model floor, OpenRouter mistralai/ministral-3b-2512 at USD 0.10/0.10 per 1M, because the author's own list price (USD 0.038 per 1M input) is below that floor; the schema head generates no text, so output tokens are 0.
source_note: 4 self-hosted systems measured on the fresh regular draw v1.6-regular-20261012 (seeded rotation-ledger draw of 1,200 sealed items + the 300-item epoch public set; drawn 2026-10-12T01:32:59Z after v1.6-regular-20261010-a2 shipped; its sealed set does not overlap that draw). One score_v16.py invocation, unmodified frozen path, JEV_NOUL_METHOD=O1S, B=1000, seed 16, no fixed G_med: this release carries its own field median, which later releases on this draw hold fixed. Scored by jevbench-add-requests-20260919 as release owner (board #17903, #17913).

systems.author: guru0381

cost.basis: v1.5-M2 base-model reference: frozen DeepInfra snapshot jevbench-v15-measure-20260925 receipts/DEEPINFRA-MODELS-20260925.json (SHA-256 84eb7926acd4e93b71d695be24898e2ca999b20011d1b66cc0348ce7c6c3546f); listing Qwen/Qwen3.5-2B, USD 0.02/M input and USD 0.10/M output. The released checkpoint names Qwen/Qwen3.5-2B-Base; the frozen DeepInfra listing omits the -Base suffix. The requester cited the Qwen3.5-4B USD 0.03/M input reference, but the matching 2B family listing is used here (precedent classone-qwen3.5-2b). Self-hosted GPU deployment has no provider tariff, so price_kind is estimate. Kev generates no free-form text. However, kev/api.py output_tokens() tokenizes JSON-serialized answers, so reported usage.output_tokens is nonzero for normal answers; it is not zero by construction.

Kev reports usage.output_tokens as the token count of the serialized answer JSON (nothing is generated); priced as reported at the reference output rate.
